chapter_metadata.description: Core suture concepts, classification, and technique illustrations.

blocks.text: Suturing is a fundamental surgical skill used to approximate tissues to promote healing, control bleeding, and restore anatomical continuity. Proper suturing minimizes infection, scarring, and tissue damage.
Suture: A material used to ligate blood vessels or approximate tissues.
Ligature: A suture used specifically to tie off blood vessels.
Absorbable suture: Broken down by the body over time.
Non-absorbable suture: Not degraded; may need removal.
Monofilament: Single strand (less infection risk).
Multifilament (braided): Multiple strands (better handling, higher infection risk).
Tensile strength: Ability to resist breaking.
Knot security: Ability of a knot to stay tied without slipping.
Needle holder: Instrument used to hold the needle during suturing.
